description: This is a false-colour infrared satellite image depicting a landscape dominated by water bodies and various types of vegetation. Healthy, dense vegetation appears in shades of dark red, indicating strong Near-Infrared (NIR) reflection, characteristic of forests or mature shrubland. Water bodies, including a winding river and several smaller channels, appear in dark blue. Linear, light blue/white features crossing the water are visible, suggesting bridges or causeways. Interspersed within the darker red vegetated areas are lighter, textured red patches, which represent areas of less dense vegetation, regenerating forest, or possibly abandoned agricultural land with recolonizing trees and shrubs, consistent with descriptions like "Clear-cuts in forest areas," "Forest regrowth areas," or "Young forest plantations." A prominent yellow arrow points to one such lighter red, textured area adjacent to the main river, on the inside bend of a river curve. This area displays a distinct texture of linear patterns within it, suggesting managed or disturbed land undergoing ecological succession. No scale bar or text labels are present.
